name: Listener crossword No 3: An Indian Crossword

clue.text: Hunted in India.

definitions.text: Hunted in India

blocks.note: the clue names a quarry, an animal chased for sport
the setter means the wild pig ridden down with spears in pig-sticking, a favourite sport of the Raj

explanation.walkthrough: This 1930 Indian puzzle is a general-knowledge crossword, so each clue is a straight definition and the crossing letters settle the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pig was the classic quarry of pig-sticking, hunted on horseback with lances by British officers in India.

clue.text: A town in the Punjab near Delhi.

definitions.text: A town in the Punjab near Delhi

blocks.note: a place in the old British province of the Punjab, which then reached to Delhi's borders
the setter means the district town some forty miles north-west of the capital

explanation.walkthrough: A straight geographical definition; the town is now in the state of Haryana, which was carved out of the Punjab in 1966.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the headquarters of a district lying just north-west of Delhi, in the Punjab as the province stood in 1930.

clue.text: Site of an old town in Malabar.

definitions.text: Site of an old town in Malabar

blocks.note: the clue asks for a place with a long history as a trading port
Malabar is used loosely for India's western coast, where this ancient port lay

explanation.walkthrough: The fourth letter is unchecked; the town is the ancient western-coast port near Bombay, and the clue stretches Malabar to cover the whole coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient harbour town on India's west coast was a known trading port in classical and medieval times.

clue.text: A railway junction between Lahore and Delhi.

definitions.text: A railway junction between Lahore and Delhi

blocks.note: a station where lines meet
the setter means the junction on the North Western Railway main line, where the route to Delhi via Meerut leaves

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the town is in the United Provinces, on the trunk railway linking Lahore with Delhi.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in the United Provinces is an important railway junction on the main line from Lahore to Delhi.

clue.text: A once famous island town in the state of Mysore.

definitions.text: A once famous island town in the state of Mysore

blocks.note: a fortress town on an island in a river, famous in the past
the setter means Tipu Sultan's capital on the Kaveri, stormed by the British in 1799

explanation.walkthrough: A straight historical definition; the town stands on an island in the Kaveri river and was Tipu Sultan's capital until its fall in 1799.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipu Sultan's island fortress capital on the Kaveri river, in Mysore, became famous when the British stormed it in 1799.

clue.text: A collection of native States under the supervision of an agent resident at Indore (three words).

definitions.text: A collection of native States under the supervision of an agent resident at Indore

blocks.note: a grouping of princely states ruled by Indian princes

blocks.clueFragment: under the supervision of an agent resident at Indore
blocks.note: the setter means the political body whose British agent sat at Indore and oversaw the states of central India

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition of a political unit of British India; its Agent to the Governor-General lived at Indore.
explanation.definitionFit: This political grouping of princely states in central India was supervised by a British Agent to the Governor-General based at Indore.

clue.text: The native name of Persia originally applied to part of India.

definitions.text: The native name of Persia originally applied to part of India

blocks.note: what Persians themselves call their country

blocks.clueFragment: originally applied to part of India
blocks.note: the setter reflects the old idea that the Aryan homeland name once covered lands reaching into north-west India

explanation.walkthrough: In 1930 the country was still officially Persia in English; it asked foreigners to use the native name only in 1935.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persians' own name for their country, from the ancient word for the land of the Aryans, which covered a wider region.

clue.text: A town in Central India near Jubbulpore.

definitions.text: A town in Central India near Jubbulpore

blocks.note: a place in the Central India Agency
the setter means the capital of a small princely state on the railway north of Jubbulpore (Jabalpur)

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the town was the seat of a small princely state, on the line between Jubbulpore and Allahabad.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the chief town of a minor princely state in central India, on the railway north of Jubbulpore.

clue.text: A dak bungalow on the way to Kashmir.

definitions.text: A dak bungalow on the way to Kashmir

blocks.note: a dak bungalow is a government rest house for travellers on a post road
the setter means a stage on the Jhelum valley road from Murree into Kashmir

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; travellers on the Jhelum valley road broke their journey at the rest house in this village before reaching Srinagar.
explanation.definitionFit: This village on the Jhelum valley road had a government rest house used by travellers heading for Srinagar.

clue.text: An exclamation.

definitions.text: An exclamation

blocks.note: the clue asks for one example
the setter means a short cry of surprise or realisation

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the crossing letters choose this cry from the many possible ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-letter interjection voicing surprise, relief or understanding is a common example of a cry.

clue.text: A railway junction in the Central Provinces.

definitions.text: A railway junction in the Central Provinces

blocks.note: a station where lines meet
the setter means the junction where the Bombay line to Jubbulpore meets the line north to Agra and Delhi

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the Central Provinces were a British province roughly matching today's Madhya Pradesh.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in the Central Provinces is a major railway junction where the Bombay-Calcutta and Delhi-Madras routes cross.

clue.text: An Indian tree.

definitions.text: An Indian tree

blocks.note: any tree growing in India
the setter means the tall hardwood of the northern forests, prized for its timber

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; this is the crossword's stock three-letter Indian tree, Shorea robusta.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorea robusta is a large hardwood forming great forests across northern India, valued for durable timber.

clue.text: Steps down to a river.

definitions.text: Steps down to a river

blocks.note: a flight of stairs
the setter means the stone landing stairs used for bathing, washing and cremation, as at Benares

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition of an Anglo-Indian word; the same word also names a mountain pass or range.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian usage the word names a flight of stone stairs leading to a riverbank, used by bathers.

clue.text: A not infrequent occurrence in India.

definitions.text: A not infrequent occurrence in India

blocks.note: something that happens fairly often
the setter means armed conflict, frequent on the North-West Frontier

explanation.walkthrough: A straight, rather vague definition; the crossing letters settle it, and the frontier campaigns of the Raj give it point.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict, especially the tribal campaigns on the North-West Frontier, was a recurring event in British India.

clue.text: A town in Baltistan (an h has been added to the ordinary spelling).

definitions.text: A town in Baltistan

blocks.note: Baltistan is the high mountain region on the upper Indus, then part of Kashmir

blocks.clueFragment: an h has been added to the ordinary spelling
blocks.note: the setter warns that the usual six-letter name is spelt here with an extra letter

explanation.walkthrough: The ordinary spelling is Skardu; the clue admits that the grid version carries an extra h to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltistan's chief town stands on the Indus, and is better known in the six-letter spelling without the h.

clue.text: Junction for Dehra Dun.

definitions.text: Junction for Dehra Dun

blocks.note: a railway station where lines meet
the setter means the station on the main line where the branch through Hardwar to Dehra Dun begins

explanation.walkthrough: The town is usually spelt Laksar; the crossing letters need this older spelling with an h.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch railway through Hardwar to Dehra Dun leaves the Oudh and Rohilkhand main line at this station.

clue.text: India's greatest neighbour

definitions.text: India's greatest neighbour

blocks.note: the clue asks about the countries bordering India
the setter means the largest country on India's borders

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; greatest here means largest in size and population.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the Himalayas lies the largest and most populous country sharing a frontier with India.

clue.text: The name of a town in Sind.

definitions.text: The name of a town in Sind

blocks.note: the clue asks for a place-name
Sind is the lower Indus province, now in Pakistan; the setter means a small town there known for glazed pottery

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the town lies north of Hyderabad in Sind and is famous for its tiles and pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A small town in the Hyderabad district of Sind, celebrated for its blue glazed tiles and pottery.

clue.text: Insert an A and this is what every Indian servant looks forward to.

definitions.text: Insert an A and this is what every Indian servant looks forward to

blocks.note: the grid word lacks one letter of the word the setter has in mind

blocks.clueFragment: what every Indian servant looks forward to
blocks.note: the setter means the servant's wages, the Hindustani word talab, pay

explanation.walkthrough: Talab is Hindustani for pay; adding an A to the grid's four letters, between the L and the B, makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindustani talab means salary or wages, which a household servant awaits at each month's end.

clue.text: Part of 7 down.

definitions.text: Part of 7 down

blocks.note: a piece of a longer word
the setter means the final four letters of the Vedic treatise at 7 down

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is simply the last four letters of UPANISHAD, read off 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The final four letters of the Vedic treatise name at 7 down form a fragment of that longer word.

clue.text: A fairly frequent phenomenon in India, esp. in the 'cold weather'

definitions.text: A fairly frequent phenomenon in India, esp. in the 'cold weather'

blocks.clueFragment: A fairly frequent phenomenon in India
blocks.note: some weather event common in India
the cold weather was the Anglo-Indian name for the cool winter season; the setter means its storms of ice pellets

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the cold weather was the Raj name for the cool season from November to February.
explanation.definitionFit: Showers of ice pellets are common in northern India, especially in winter and spring thunderstorms.

clue.text: A place in the hills of Ceylon.

definitions.text: A place in the hills of Ceylon

blocks.note: the clue asks for a locality
Ceylon is today's Sri Lanka; the setter means a tea district in its central highlands

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the place is a tea-planting district near Nuwara Eliya in the central hills of Ceylon, now Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tea-estate district in the central highlands of Ceylon, near the hill station of Nuwara Eliya.

clue.text: Add two letters and you get a welcome sound which Lucknow heard in 1857.

definitions.text: Add two letters and you get a welcome sound which Lucknow heard in 1857

blocks.note: the grid word is two letters short of the word the setter has in mind

blocks.clueFragment: a welcome sound which Lucknow heard in 1857
blocks.note: the setter means the Highland bagpipe music heard as relief reached the besieged Residency

explanation.walkthrough: Adding CH completes PIBROCH, the bagpipe music of the Highlanders whose approach heralded the relief of besieged Lucknow in 1857.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the besieged garrison at Lucknow heard Highland pipes playing as the relieving force approached.

clue.text: A familiar military cart.

definitions.text: A familiar military cart

blocks.note: a wagon well known to soldiers
the setter means the Army Transport cart, known by its initials

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the initials of Army Transport, which gave its name to the standard mule cart of the Indian Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian Army's standard two-wheeled mule cart was known by the initials of Army Transport.

clue.text: A rest house.

definitions.text: A rest house

blocks.note: a building where travellers stop
the setter means the walled inn for caravans and travellers found along Indian roads

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; this is the Hindustani form of caravanserai, spelt with A where English often writes serai.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and Persia a walled lodging for travellers and their animals, the caravanserai, bears this name.

clue.text: A small coin.

definitions.text: A small coin

blocks.note: a piece of money of low value
the setter means the smallest Indian copper, a twelfth of an anna

explanation.walkthrough: The Indian pie, worth a twelfth of an anna, is spelt here in its short form to fit two cells.
explanation.definitionFit: The pie was the smallest Indian copper coin, worth one twelfth of an anna or a third of a pice.

clue.text: A great part of Rajputana is this.

definitions.text: A great part of Rajputana is this

blocks.note: Rajputana is the region of princely states now forming Rajasthan
the setter wants an adjective describing the Thar desert country

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; much of Rajputana, now Rajasthan, is the Thar desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thar desert covers much of Rajputana, so most of the region is dry, with scanty rainfall.

clue.text: A large number.

definitions.text: A large number

blocks.note: a big quantity
the setter means the Indian unit for one hundred thousand

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition of the Indian numbering word for a hundred thousand, also spelt lakh.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian reckoning this word denotes one hundred thousand, written 1,00,000.

clue.text: A resin.

definitions.text: A resin

blocks.note: the clue asks for one kind
the setter means the resinous secretion of an insect, the raw material of a common varnish

explanation.walkthrough: The same word as 56 across in a different sense; India was the chief source of this insect resin, refined into shellac.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale insect's secretion on Indian trees is refined into a varnish and sealing wax.

clue.text: A fairly common termination of Indian names.

definitions.text: A fairly common termination of Indian names

blocks.note: an ending found on many words
the setter means the ending of names such as Badrinath and Amarnath

explanation.walkthrough: Names ending in -nath (lord), such as Badrinath, Kedarnath and Somnath, are common in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Indian place and personal names end with these letters, as in Somnath, Badrinath and Jagannath.

clue.text: Treacherous in India as many flyers have found.

definitions.text: Treacherous in India as many flyers have found

blocks.note: something dangerous in India
the setter means the bumpy, hot atmosphere early aviators met over India

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; pilots of the 1920s found India's hot, turbulent atmosphere dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere over India, with heat bumps and dust storms, was notoriously dangerous for early aviators.

clue.text: Some think that India can never be this.

definitions.text: Some think that India can never be this

blocks.note: the clue reports an opinion
the setter means united as a single nation, a live debate in 1930

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; in 1930 many argued that India's many peoples could never form a single united nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means united or single, as in the doubt whether India's many peoples could form a single nation.

clue.text: A famous pass in Baluchistan.

definitions.text: A famous pass in Baluchistan

blocks.note: a well-known mountain route
the setter means the route from Sibi up to Quetta, used by armies and caravans

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the pass carries the road and railway from the Indus plain up to Quetta.
explanation.definitionFit: This historic mountain route links the Indus plain with Quetta, and was used by invaders and traders.

clue.text: An exclamation.

definitions.text: An exclamation

blocks.note: the clue asks for one example
the setter means a short cry of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the crossing letters choose which cry is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-letter interjection voicing surprise or dismay is a common example of a cry.

clue.text: Army Temperance Association.

definitions.text: Army Temperance Association

blocks.note: a movement against drink among soldiers
the setter wants the society's initials

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the initials of the Army Temperance Association, a society that ran teetotal clubs for British soldiers in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials stand for the society that promoted abstinence from drink among British troops in India.

clue.text: A well-known inlet of the Arabian sea.

definitions.text: A well-known inlet of the Arabian sea

blocks.note: an arm of the sea reaching inland
the setter means the salt marsh of Cutch, flooded by the sea in the monsoon

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the Rann of Cutch is a vast salt marsh that the Arabian sea floods in the monsoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rann of Cutch is a great salt flat on India's west coast, seasonally flooded by the sea.

clue.text: Second half of the name of a well-known railway terminus.

definitions.text: Second half of the name of a well-known railway terminus

blocks.note: only the latter part of a longer name is wanted
the setter means the great East Indian Railway terminus across the Hooghly from Calcutta

explanation.walkthrough: The terminus is Howrah, Calcutta's main station; its last three letters fill the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The final three letters of the name of Calcutta's great railway station on the Hooghly form the latter part of it.

clue.text: A district in Southern India.

definitions.text: A district in Southern India

blocks.note: a region or territory
the setter means the historic region of the south-east coastal plain, scene of Clive's wars

explanation.walkthrough: Usually spelt Carnatic; the region is the coastal plain of the south-east, scene of the eighteenth-century Anglo-French wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to the region between the Eastern Ghats and the Coromandel coast, ruled by the Nawabs of Arcot.

clue.text: A treatise forming part of the Vedas.

definitions.text: A treatise forming part of the Vedas

blocks.note: a written work on a subject
the Vedas are the oldest Hindu scriptures; the setter means one of their philosophical closing texts

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; these philosophical texts close the Vedas and are the basis of Vedanta.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of these Sanskrit philosophical texts forms the concluding portion of a Veda, the Hindu scriptures.

clue.text: Indians distinguished themselves at this siege.

definitions.text: Indians distinguished themselves at this siege

blocks.note: Indian troops fought with credit
the setter means the Mesopotamian town besieged by the Turks in 1915-16, held by an Anglo-Indian force

explanation.walkthrough: Kut-al-Amara in Mesopotamia was held by Townshend's largely Indian division for nearly five months before surrendering in April 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: Townshend's Indian division withstood a long siege in this town on the Tigris before surrendering in 1916.

clue.text: A small Indian weight.

definitions.text: A small Indian weight

blocks.note: a modest quantity
the setter means the unit of about two pounds, a fortieth of a maund

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; this Indian unit of weight was about two pounds, a fortieth of a maund.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian unit of weight, roughly two pounds, was one fortieth of a maund.

clue.text: You will find this in forts in India.

definitions.text: You will find this in forts in India

blocks.note: something present
the setter means the gunners who manned coastal and frontier fortresses, given by their initials

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is initials: the Royal Garrison Artillery manned the heavy guns of fortresses across the Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Garrison Artillery was the branch of the British gunners that manned fortress guns, including Indian forts.

clue.text: A title of honour.

definitions.text: A title of honour

blocks.note: a style given to a person
the setter means the distinction conferred by the British government on Hindus, as in Bahadur

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the title, often with Bahadur added, was conferred on Hindu gentlemen by the government of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The government of British India granted this honorific to Hindu notables, often in the fuller form with Bahadur.

clue.text: First part of the name of a famous Indian regiment, of horse.

definitions.text: First part of the name of a famous Indian regiment, of horse

blocks.note: only the opening letters of a name are wanted

blocks.clueFragment: a famous Indian regiment, of horse
blocks.note: the setter means the cavalry regiment raised in Sind and named after the province's old spelling

explanation.walkthrough: The regiment is the Scinde Horse, named from the old spelling of Sind; the grid takes its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening three letters of the Scinde Horse, a celebrated Indian cavalry regiment, are an initial portion of its name.

clue.text: Hindustani for 'that much'.

definitions.text: Hindustani for 'that much'

blocks.note: the clue asks for a word in the common language of northern India
the setter means the word of quantity used for so much or this much

explanation.walkthrough: A straight translation clue; Hindustani was the everyday language of northern India, spoken by most British residents.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindustani this word expresses quantity, meaning so much or as much as this.

clue.text: Hindustani for 'cupboard'.

definitions.text: Hindustani for 'cupboard'

blocks.note: the clue asks for a word in the common language of northern India
the setter means the free-standing wardrobe of Anglo-Indian homes

explanation.walkthrough: The word came into Hindustani from the Portuguese armario and passed into Anglo-Indian English.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from Portuguese, this word names a movable wardrobe or chest of shelves in Indian households.

clue.text: Transfer the last two letters and add 'u' and you get the name of a dish made of chicken.

definitions.text: Transfer the last two letters and add 'u' and you get the name of a dish made of chicken

blocks.clueFragment: Transfer the last two letters and add 'u'
blocks.note: swapping the final pair of letters and adding a letter turns the grid word into another

blocks.clueFragment: the name of a dish made of chicken
blocks.note: the setter means the spiced rice dish, here with chicken

explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the last two letters gives PILA, and adding U gives PILAU, the spiced rice dish; the grid word itself is a South Indian name for a raised verandah.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue defines only by transformation: the grid word, reshuffled at its end and extended, becomes the rice dish pilau.

clue.text: Termination meaning meadow.

definitions.text: Termination meaning meadow

blocks.note: an ending of place-names
the setter means the Kashmiri word that closes the names of famous hill resorts

explanation.walkthrough: In Kashmir, place-names such as Gulmarg (meadow of flowers) and Sonamarg end with this word for meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kashmiri place-names this ending signifies a high grassy pasture, as in Gulmarg.

clue.text: A town in Assam.

definitions.text: A town in Assam

blocks.note: a place-name
Assam is the province of north-east India; the setter means its chief town on the Brahmaputra

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the town, now spelt Guwahati, stands on the Brahmaputra.
explanation.definitionFit: This river port on the Brahmaputra is the largest town of Assam, today spelt Guwahati.

clue.text: A capital of the Moghul Empire for many years.

definitions.text: A capital of the Moghul Empire for many years

blocks.clueFragment: A capital of the Moghul Empire
blocks.note: one of the seats of the Mughal emperors
the setter means the city on the Jumna that served as capital under Akbar and his successors

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the city on the Jumna, home of the Taj Mahal, was the Mughal capital for much of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan ruled from this city on the Jumna before the court moved to Delhi.

clue.text: A town in the Punjab famous for its engineering college.

definitions.text: A town in the Punjab famous for its engineering college

blocks.note: a place in northern India
the setter means the seat of the Thomason Civil Engineering College, founded 1847

explanation.walkthrough: Usually spelt Roorkee; the Thomason College there was India's first engineering college. It actually lay in the United Provinces, near the Punjab border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thomason College of Civil Engineering, India's oldest, was founded at this town in 1847.

clue.text: A peak in the Himalayas, 26,825 feet high.

definitions.text: A peak in the Himalayas, 26,825 feet high

blocks.note: a great mountain of the range
the setter means the Nepalese summit given about this height in the surveys of the day

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the Nepalese peak was then credited with about 26,825 feet and is now put at 26,795.
explanation.definitionFit: This massif in Nepal, whose name means white mountain, is the world's seventh-highest summit.

clue.text: Possible initials of a telegraph company.

definitions.text: Possible initials of a telegraph company

blocks.note: a set of letters standing for a name
the setter means letters that could stand for something like Eastern Indian Telegraph

explanation.walkthrough: The setter admits these are only plausible initials, such as Eastern Indian Telegraph; the crossing letters fix them.
explanation.definitionFit: The three letters could abbreviate a cable firm's name beginning Eastern and ending Telegraph.

clue.text: A title meaning a minor ruler.

definitions.text: A title meaning a minor ruler

blocks.note: a style given to a person
the setter means the Muslim title for a provincial governor or prince

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the word originally meant a deputy governing for the Mughal emperor, and gave English nabob.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a Mughal deputy governor, the title came to mean a Muslim prince ruling a small state.

clue.text: Hindustani for four.

definitions.text: Hindustani for four

blocks.note: the clue asks for a word in the common language of northern India
the setter wants the numeral

explanation.walkthrough: A straight translation clue; the word survives in English in charpoy, a four-legged bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindustani numeral for 4, familiar from charpoy, the four-legged string bed.

clue.text: A tributary of the Brahmaputra.

definitions.text: A tributary of the Brahmaputra

blocks.note: a river feeding a larger one
the setter means the Tibetan river reckoned in 1930 to feed the great river of Assam

explanation.walkthrough: The Yaru (Yarlung) Tsangpo of Tibet is really the Brahmaputra's upper course, which the setter counts as a feeder; the second letter is unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tibetan river flows east through Tibet and becomes the great river of Assam after cutting through the Himalayas.

clue.text: A junction on the East Indian Railway.

definitions.text: A junction on the East Indian Railway

blocks.note: a railway station where lines meet
the setter means the coalfield junction in Bengal on the main line out of Calcutta

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the town is the hub of the Raniganj coalfield in Bengal, on the East Indian Railway's main line from Calcutta.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bengal coalfield town is a major junction on the East Indian Railway's main line from Calcutta.

clue.text: A town in the U.P. with an anomalous name.

definitions.text: A town in the U.P. with an anomalous name

blocks.note: U.P. stands for the United Provinces, today's Uttar Pradesh
the setter means a holy Hindu city that bears a Muslim name meaning abode of God

explanation.walkthrough: The anomaly is that the great Hindu pilgrimage city at the meeting of the Ganges and Jumna bears the Muslim name Akbar gave it.
explanation.definitionFit: Akbar renamed the Hindu holy city of Prayag at the Ganges-Jumna confluence with an Islamic name, City of God.

clue.text: A cantonment in the Himalayas famous for an earthquake.

definitions.text: A cantonment in the Himalayas famous for an earthquake

blocks.note: a cantonment is a permanent military station; the clue wants a hill one
the setter means the Kangra valley station destroyed by the earthquake of 1905

explanation.walkthrough: A straight definition; the Gurkha cantonment in the Kangra valley was wrecked by the 1905 Kangra earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kangra hill station housed a Gurkha garrison and was devastated by the great earthquake of April 1905.

clue.text: Hindustani for 'black'.

definitions.text: Hindustani for 'black'

blocks.note: the clue asks for a word in the common language of northern India
the setter wants the colour word

explanation.walkthrough: A straight translation clue; the word appears in kala-azar, black fever, and kala pani, the black water of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindustani adjective for the darkest colour, seen in kala-azar, the black fever.

clue.text: An Indian Governor.

definitions.text: An Indian Governor

blocks.note: the clue asks for a title used in India
the setter means some word for a provincial ruler; the usual three-letter crossword choice, the Hindustani lat, does not fit the crossing letters

explanation.walkthrough: UNRESOLVED: the crossings give S then L, with the last cell unchecked, and no known title for a governor fits. This fill is a placeholder until the published solution corrects it.
